svg.aria-label: Diagram: how Access Context Manager defines conditions that other services enforce, why conditions short-circuit and a condition that raises a runtime error is ignored rather than denied, the two different combining rules where attributes within a level are ANDed while levels bound to a group are ORed, and the documented limits and exemptions of context-aware access
svg.title: Context-aware access: conditions defined in one service, enforced in another, ignored when they error
svg.text: A condition that fails to evaluate is not a denial. It is a no-op.
And the levels bound to a group are ORed, so each one you add widens access rather than narrowing it.
Access Context Manager defines conditions. It does not enforce them.
Access Context Manager is designed to define specific rules or context.
Policy is configured and enforced across various points, such as VPC Service Controls.
Enforcement points: VPC Service Controls, Identity-Aware Proxy, CAA for Workspace, IAM conditions.
And these checks are applied IN ADDITION TO standard IAM policy, never instead of it.
Conditions short-circuit, and a condition that ERRORS is ignored
If one operand uniquely determines the result, the other might or might not be evaluated.
And if that evaluation produces a runtime error, IT IS IGNORED.
Google worked example: region check FAILED, IP check GRANTED, combined with OR gives GRANTED.
So a broken condition is not a denial. It is a no-op that the OR then votes past.
Two different combining rules — one tightens, one loosens
WITHIN a basic access level: attributes combine as AND (all true) or NOR (none true).
ACROSS the levels bound to a group: multiple access levels are logically ORed.
So adding another access level to a binding WIDENS access. Satisfying any one is enough.
What it cannot see, and who sits outside it
Data Studio is always allowed unrestricted access to the Google Cloud APIs, regardless of policy.
No device attributes for non-Google OAuth clients. No IP attribute for Docker connections.
Applies only to users within your organization, and the docs advise excluding an Org Admin
from the bound group, to reduce the risk of an accidental lockout.
Targeted by binding a GOOGLE GROUP to access levels, so #52 applies: membership decides, and
a binding takes minutes to propagate. Device attributes need paid Chrome Enterprise Premium.
#51 the front door had an exemption. #52 the unit of access revoked in hours. #53 the conditions
are defined in one service, enforced in another, and ignored entirely when they error.
